rule.body: To spot an error, find the subject and its verb first, then check the tense, preposition, pronoun and question tag. Watch common slips: say 'switch off the light', not 'off the light'; 'lend me', not 'borrow me'; 'discuss the matter', not 'discuss about'; 'cope with', not 'cope up with'. After a preposition such as 'between', use 'me', not 'I'. A negative word such as 'hardly' takes a positive tag.
rule.example: Could you lend me your pen? (not 'borrow me your pen')

questions.stem: Please [[off the light]] before you go to bed. Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part.
questions.explanation: 'Off' is not a verb here; we switch off (or turn off) a light.

questions.stem: Could you [[borrow me]] your pen for a minute? Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part.
questions.explanation: You lend something to someone and borrow something from someone, so the owner says 'lend me'.

questions.stem: We will [[discuss about]] the matter tomorrow. Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part.
questions.explanation: 'Discuss' takes a direct object with no preposition: discuss the matter.

questions.stem: Students must learn to [[cope up with]] pressure. Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part.
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'cope with'; 'up' is not used with it.

questions.stem: The list of names [[are]] on the notice board. Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'list', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'. 'Of names' does not change the subject.

questions.stem: He hardly visits his parents, [[doesn't he]]? Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' makes the sentence negative, so the tag is positive; 'visits' is present simple, so 'does he'.

questions.stem: By the time we arrived, the train [[has left]]. Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part.
questions.explanation: The train left before another past action (we arrived), so the past perfect 'had left' is needed.

questions.stem: Please speak louder; I [[am not hearing]] you. Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part.
questions.explanation: 'Hear' is a verb of perception and is normally used with 'can', not in the -ing form: I cannot hear you.

questions.stem: Between you and [[I]], the plan will not work. Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part.
questions.explanation: 'Between' is a preposition, so it takes the object pronoun 'me'.

questions.stem: No sooner had we sat down [[when]] the rain started. Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' is always followed by 'than': No sooner had we sat down than the rain started.
